q: Did games with smaller crowds coincide with smaller national TV audiences in 2025 and 2026?
report:
No, there was no clear link showing that smaller crowds coincided with smaller national TV audiences in 2025 and 2026 once each game was compared to its own park's usual crowd, though raw crowds and TV audiences did move together moderately. Comparing games on the same network in 2025, crowds and national TV audiences moved together moderately (correlation 0.34, n = 82, range 0.14 to 0.52) (table: crowd_tv_residual). After comparing each game with its own park's usual crowd, so popular teams do not drive the result, the correlation is 0.16 (range -0.05 to 0.37), so there is no clear link (table: crowd_tv_residual). Comparing games on the same network in 2026, crowds and national TV audiences moved together moderately (correlation 0.47, n = 83, range 0.29 to 0.62) (table: crowd_tv_residual). After comparing each game with its own park's usual crowd, so popular teams do not drive the result, the correlation is 0.14 (range -0.08 to 0.34), so there is no clear link (table: crowd_tv_residual).

*Viewership figures are publicly reported and may differ from official Nielsen data. They are the national TV audience, excluding streaming add-ons. Nielsen changed its method on September 1, 2025, so 2025 and 2026 figures are not like-for-like. These are associations, not cause and effect.*

q: Why did the Mets over-perform on attendance in 2025?
report:
We cannot determine the exact cause of the New York Mets' attendance over-performance in 2025 because our data only tracks coinciding events rather than direct cause and effect. The New York Mets averaged 39,776 a game in 2025, up 35.9% from 29,268 the season before. That is 23.6% above the 32,182 that the prior two years of crowds, win rate and market would predict. Part of this may be a rebound: the team was 18.8% below its prediction the season before. (table: team_season_model) This high turnout coincided with the Mets signing outfielder Juan Soto to a 15-year, $765 million contract in December 2024, representing the largest contract in professional sports history ([2025 New York Mets season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_New_York_Mets_season)). The strong season also coincided with the team opening the year with a 45–24 record through June 12, marking the second-most wins through the first 70 games in franchise history ([2025 New York Mets season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_New_York_Mets_season)). Additionally, the Mets retired David Wright's number 5 and inducted him into the team's Hall of Fame during a pre-game ceremony on July 19 ([2025 New York Mets season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_New_York_Mets_season)).

*Promotions are not in the data. These are associations, not cause and effect.*

q: Do Cubs Sunday games draw better than their Tuesday games?
report: Yes, Chicago Cubs Sunday home games consistently draw larger crowds than Tuesday home games. Across the 2024, 2025, and 2026 seasons, Sunday home games averaged 37,140 fans, while Tuesday home games averaged 35,280 fans (table: games_clean). This trend of Sundays drawing better than Tuesdays held true for the Cubs across all three individual seasons (table: games_clean). In 2024, Sunday home games averaged 36,916 fans over 14 games, while Tuesdays averaged 34,367 fans over 12 games (table: games_clean). In 2025, Sunday home games averaged 37,262 fans over 14 games, while Tuesdays averaged 35,802 fans over 13 games (table: games_clean). In 2026, Sundays averaged 37,260 fans over 12 games, while Tuesdays averaged 35,602 fans over 13 games (table: games_clean).

q: What was the attendance at the Speedway Classic?
report: The attendance at the Speedway Classic game between the Cincinnati Reds and Atlanta Braves on August 2, 2025, was 91,032 (table: games). This turnout of 91,032 set a new all-time regular-season MLB game attendance record ([MLB Speedway Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MLB_Speedway_Classic)). The matchup at Bristol Motor Speedway in Bristol, Tennessee, was the first regular-season National League or American League game played in the state of Tennessee and the first MLB game ever played on a racetrack ([MLB Speedway Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MLB_Speedway_Classic)). Construction for the specialty game began in late June 2025, featuring an AstroTurf artificial turf surface with a traditional dirt infield built across the speedway's layout between Turns 3 and 4 ([MLB Speedway Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MLB_Speedway_Classic)).

Major League Baseball attendance fluctuations coincide with home openers, the day of the week, the opponent, and a team's winning percentage and historical crowd sizes. Home openers coincide with a 69.1% increase in attendance (table: model_coefficients). For opponents, games against the Los Angeles Dodgers coincide with a 25.0% increase and games against the New York Yankees with a 15.7% increase compared to the average opponent, while matchups with the Miami Marlins and Colorado Rockies coincide with decreases of 6.6% and 6.5% respectively (table: model_coefficients). Day of the week differences also coincide with attendance changes compared to Friday: Saturday games see an 8.8% increase, while Monday games see the largest decrease at 21.8%, followed by Wednesday (-20.6%), Tuesday (-18.9%), Thursday (-16.6%), and Sunday (-1.0%) (table: model_coefficients). Monthly attendance compared to August is highest in July (+4.2%) and June (+2.5%), while March and April games see a 10.9% decrease (table: model_coefficients). At the team level, a season win rate .100 higher coincides with an 8.6% increase in attendance, and a prior two-year crowd 10% higher coincides with an 8.2% increase (table: model_coefficients). However, a metro population 10% larger only coincides with a 0.2% increase after accounting for prior crowds, which is not a clear effect (table: model_coefficients).

*These are associations, not cause and effect.*
